upstream_expectation: the JSON-LD 1.0 "List conversion" output (option.specVersion=json-ld-1.0): 1.0 converted an RDF collection to @list node-by-node against triples that are only PARTIALLY ORDERED on purpose (see the manifest `purpose`), yielding the specific partially-collapsed shape 0008-out.jsonld pins
our_expectation: the JSON-LD 1.1 "Serialize RDF as JSON-LD" list conversion — a single order-independent referenced-once/list-shape pass — which fully collapses the same input and so does NOT reproduce the 1.0-only partial shape
rationale: This is the sole specVersion=json-ld-1.0 fromRdf fixture. JSONLD.FromRdf implements the JSON-LD 1.1 fully-collapsing RDF-collection-to-@list algorithm; t0008 pins the 1.0 partially-ordered conversion, so our output legitimately differs. The same 1.0-vs-1.1 gap is what the toRdf runner records as an honest specVersion skip. The suite's OWN #tli03 ("t0008 as interpreted for 1.1") pins the 1.1 fully-collapsed shape and passes here — so the 1.1 reading is not our invention, it is the corpus's own 1.1 expectation for this input. Previously carried as a specVersion=json-ld-1.0 skip in jsonld_fromrdf_runner.ml; converted to a local-override on 2026-07-17 so the test runs and its disagreement is counted distinctly rather than hidden.
owner_directive: if we carefully disagree with test make our own local override of it. Shex Also. (owner, 2026-07-17)
